contribution.name: Technocore HTTPS-origin validation hardening
contribution.motivation: The client accepted credentials, paths, queries, and fragments in its base URL even though it appends Technocore's root-relative signed routes. A crafted value could expose embedded credentials in dry-run output or send a signed request to an unintended route.
contribution.summary: Require a pure HTTPS origin, reject credentials, non-root paths, queries, fragments, invalid ports, whitespace, and control characters, and cover both validation and signed-route construction with regression tests.

validation.reproduction: Credential-bearing and path-bearing base URLs are rejected before the signed-message route builder can return a URL.
validation.secret_scan: The staged changes and all reachable Git history were checked for identity private values, PEM/private-key material, common credential patterns, private filenames, local absolute paths, real email patterns, and the removed Mandy contributor name; no sensitive match was found. A generic seed-phrase wording in SECURITY.md was reviewed as documentation, not secret material.

technocore.verification: The signed write returned HTTP 200. A JSON read of sequence 6 returned the expected full did:key author, exact nonce, timestamp, commit URL, and message text.
